To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we can achieve a performance of 8 billion row scans per second on a single core, (2) that the new AVX2 instructions are a key factor for achieving this performance, and (3) that the In-List scan can be vectorized using the same techniques.
we are able to vectorize the full table scan for column stores with complex predicates using SIMD instructions and that the new AVX2 instruction-set is an important building block for this.

we have shown how the new SIMD instruction set of the Intel Haswell processors can be leveraged to vectorize column-scan with complex predicates and how the performance can be increased significantly by using a combination of different vectorization strategies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the acceleration of the column-scan, which is a fundamental operation in column-store database systems and is critical for the performance of these systems.
the acceleration of the most fundamental operation in a column-store database system.
the efficient implementation of complex predicates for column scans in database systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SIMD is not only for the few but for the many.
the new Intel AVx2 SIMD instructions provide a significant boost to the vectorized column-scan performance.
AVX2 is the new standard for column-store database systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the performance of column-scan operations is not limited by the CPU speed any more.
we have shown how a full table scan on the columnar data can be accelerated to a throughput of 8 Billion rows per second on one single core of a commodity CPU.

we have shown that the full table scan performance of column-store systems is not limited by the SIMD vectorization, but that there is a lot of room for improvement by using the latest instruction set extensions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SIMD instructions can be used to accelerate a large class of column-scan operations.
the new Intel AVx2 instruction set enables us to implement highly performant algorithms that are able to vectorize a wide range of complex predicates.
column-scan performance can be improved by a combination of hardware and software optimizations.
